activationPreconditions: protected merge SHA recorded and the plan regenerated from it
staging-only reconciliation with the protected staging administrator credential after independent plan review
the realm OTP execution configured so the AMR mapper emits mfa; until then every human CIP token fails closed on mfa
Middleware registers the proposed platform-command-client members in config/control-plane-callers.v1.json
Kong consumes this gateway contract by digest and reproduces every token-matrix verdict and status
service client secrets handed to runners only through 0600 secret files resolved from secretReference
production cip-portal remains blocked until its origin is reviewed; unbound scopes stay unbound until Middleware routes exist

authority.consumptionRule: Kong imports this file as data only, pins it by sha256 and never edits Keycloak desired state.
authority.hashRule: contractSha256, tokenMatrixSha256 and parityEvidenceSha256 are sha256 over json.dumps(document, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')).encode('utf-8'); desiredStatePlanSha256 is sha256 over the committed plan file bytes, as recorded in its .sha256 file

conformance.rule: Kong must reproduce the verdict and HTTP status of every request-level and issued-token case; refused-issuance cases are enforced by Keycloak.

enforcementOrder: signature against the environment JWKS with an allowed algorithm (401 algorithm_or_kid_denied)
exact issuer, audience contains middleware-api, iat <= now < exp, exp - iat <= 300, nbf <= now (401 invalid_token)
azp is in the environment CIP azpRegistry (403 authorized_party_denied)
codestra_actor_kind equals the registry actorKind; service tokens carry no amr (403 actor_kind_denied)
user tokens carry amr containing mfa (403 mfa_required)
no prohibited scope or role, and every token scope is in the registry allowedScopes (403 scope_denied)
the route's required scope is present in the scope claim (403 insufficient_scope)
exactly one valid tenant_id, no prohibited tenant claim, equal to the registry tenant for service accounts, and every tenant selector equals it (403 cross_tenant_denied)
every project selector is in a non-empty project_ids; service project_ids equal the registry projects (403 cross_project_denied)
forward the original bearer token; Middleware re-validates it and applies business entitlements

production.note: No CIP client is active in production: every production CIP token is rejected authorized_party_denied.

knownConsumerDrift.finding: deploy/kong/scope-policy.lua and deploy/kong/control-plane.yml read claims.tenant; the codestra-authz plugin schema allows tenant_claim tenant or org_id.
knownConsumerDrift.requiredChange: Read tenant_id only for CIP routes and treat tenant, org_id, tid, organization and tenant_ids as prohibited on CIP tokens.

knownConsumerDrift.finding: authorize_tenant and tenants_from_claims also accept tenant_ids (up to 64 tenants); there is no project dimension and no MFA check.
knownConsumerDrift.requiredChange: None required for safety (CIP tokens never carry tenant_ids); project and MFA enforcement stay at the gateway until Middleware adopts them.

projectSelectors.rule: A project value in the request is a selector only. Present requires a non-empty token project_ids that contains it exactly; otherwise the request is denied 403 cross_project_denied.

rateLimitKeys.rule: Coarse per-tenant/project abuse limits only; business quotas and entitlements stay in Middleware.
rateLimitKeys.secondary: the validated project selector, else the literal '-' (never an unvalidated header)

routeRules.boundScopes: On a BOUND route, keep the frozen per-route scope/azp checks from the Middleware authority and, when azp is a CIP registry client, add the CIP tenant/project/actor/MFA checks above.
routeRules.platformCommandFamily: The frozen caller authority keeps platform-command-client unresolved and membership-required. These staging CIP clients are proposed members only; Middleware rejects their azp on the command routes until it registers them, and Keycloak does not modify the frozen caller authority.
routeRules.unboundScopes: An UNBOUND product scope satisfies no route. Kong must not accept it anywhere until Middleware publishes a route and Keycloak repins this contract.

tenantSelectors.rule: A tenant value in the request is a selector only. Absent is allowed. Present must equal the token tenant_id exactly (case-sensitive), otherwise the request is denied 403 cross_tenant_denied. A selector never replaces, widens or adds to the token tenant.

token.audienceRule: aud is a string or an array and MUST contain middleware-api
